page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-128 is an x86_64 general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 128 vCPUs mapped to 64 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, alongside 512 GB of dedicated system memory, yielding a 4.0 GB per core ratio. The CPU architecture includes 54 MB of L3 cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 KB of L1d cache. It lacks local NVMe storage and integrated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 120717.34 and a Passmark CPU score of 84204.45, placing it in the top tier. The system demonstrates high memory bandwidth, reaching 309.76 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 135.09 GB/sec for large block write operations. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware flags like AES, VAES, SHA_NI, AVX, and AVX512F, which contribute to a strong Passmark CPU encryption test score of 104777.43.

While multi-threaded execution and memory bandwidth are strong, single-core performance is average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1541.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1844.49. Large-scale LLM text generation represents a significant performance bottleneck, with the 70B model achieving only 2.7 tokens/sec. This server is suited for highly parallelized workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and medium-scale LLM prompt processing, but is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale generative AI inference.
